descriptionReviews.proposedDescriptionDe: Die lernende Person kann konstante Beschleunigung bei geradliniger Bewegung durch gleiche vorzeichenbehaftete Geschwindigkeitsänderungen in gleichen Zeitabschnitten erklären und die t-s-, t-v- und t-a-Diagramme derselben Bewegung aufeinander beziehen.
descriptionReviews.proposedDescriptionEn: The learner can explain constant acceleration in straight-line motion in terms of equal signed changes in velocity over equal time intervals and relate the position–time, velocity–time and acceleration–time graphs of the same motion to one another.

understandingEvidence.essentialUnderstandingDe: Bei festgelegter positiver Richtung ist a = Δv/Δt im Modellintervall konstant. Dieser Wert ist die Steigung der Geraden im t-v-Diagramm und die Höhe der waagerechten Linie im t-a-Diagramm. Im t-s-Diagramm gibt die Steigung zu jedem Zeitpunkt die Geschwindigkeit an. Bei positivem a ist der Ortsgraph eine nach oben, bei negativem a eine nach unten geöffnete Parabel.
understandingEvidence.essentialUnderstandingEn: For a chosen positive direction, a = Δv/Δt is constant over the modeled interval. Its value is the slope of the straight line on the velocity–time graph and the level of the horizontal line on the acceleration–time graph. The slope of the position–time graph at each instant gives the velocity. The position graph is an upward-opening parabola for positive a and a downward-opening parabola for negative a.
understandingEvidence.observablePerformanceDe: Für einen Wagen, dessen Bewegung mit konstanter Beschleunigung modelliert wird, erstellt die lernende Person aus neuen Orts- und Geschwindigkeitswerten selbstständig die drei Zeitdiagramme mit beschrifteten Achsen und Einheiten. Sie bestimmt a aus einer Geschwindigkeitsänderung und dem zugehörigen Zeitintervall und erklärt, wie sich die Anfangsgeschwindigkeit und die weitere Geschwindigkeitsänderung in den Steigungen des Ortsgraphen zeigen.
understandingEvidence.observablePerformanceEn: Given fresh position and velocity values for a cart modeled with constant acceleration, the learner independently constructs all three time graphs with labeled axes and units. They determine a from a change in velocity and the corresponding time interval and explain how the slopes of the position graph reflect the initial velocity and its subsequent change.
understandingEvidence.transferExpectationDe: In einer neuen Aufgabe erhält die lernende Person nur einen parabelförmigen t-s-Graphen mit einem Minimum innerhalb des dargestellten Zeitintervalls. Sie sagt aus den Steigungen voraus, dass der t-v-Graph als steigende Gerade die Nulllinie schneidet, und zeichnet den zugehörigen konstant positiven t-a-Graphen. Sie erklärt, warum der Körper bis zum Minimum langsamer und danach in der Gegenrichtung schneller wird.
understandingEvidence.transferExpectationEn: In a fresh task, the learner receives only a parabolic position–time graph with a minimum inside the displayed interval. From its slopes, they predict that the velocity–time graph is a rising straight line crossing zero and draw the corresponding constant positive acceleration–time graph. They explain why the object slows down until it reaches the minimum and then speeds up in the opposite direction.

descriptionReviews.rationale: The current wording names constant acceleration twice without saying what remains equal. Equal signed velocity changes over equal times give the learner a physical relationship that explains all three graphs. This is one kinematic competence across the compiled Sek I and Sek II placements and requires no formal derivation of the motion equations.

profileReviews.reason: Both model cases are numerically correct. The first gives a = +0.40 m/s² and a displacement of +0.60 m from 1 to 2 s. The second gives a = −0.50 m/s² and successive positions of 0, 0.75, 1.00, 0.75 and 0 m, with the maximum at 2 s. The two independent demonstrations change both the starting representation and the relative signs of velocity and acceleration. Both use supplied model information and require no experimental procedure. The wording needs local corrections concerning what the samples and individual graphs establish and how the required model limitation is elicited.
requiredChanges: In both languages of ‘starting-from-rest’, ask for the continuous graphs under the assumption of constant acceleration throughout 0–3 s. The samples establish equal average accelerations across the listed intervals. In the understanding focus, specify equal time intervals and tie the increasing positive displacements to this cart’s positive direction of travel.

In ‘deceleration-through-reversal’, identify what each graph shows at 2 s. Velocity crosses zero, position reaches a maximum, and acceleration stays at −0.50 m/s². The acceleration graph alone cannot locate the reversal.

In ‘linked-three-graphs’, describe calculus as unnecessary and accept any valid explanation of the graph relationships. Keep the signed velocity–time area as a displacement check and the trapezoid calculation as an example.

To cover ‘zero-velocity-and-validity’, ask in one case whether the supplied information determines the motion after the final time. The learner should explain that extrapolation would require a further assumption about acceleration.

limitations: At 3 s the primary illustration prints the velocity as “6 m//s”. The intended value is 6 m/s, consistent with its velocity–time graph.
Applicability was checked against the supplied compiled national scope. The underlying state curriculum documents and individual source-clause mappings were not independently inspected.
